newsitem.title: UK: London stock market to focus on domestic results.
newsitem.headline: London stock market to focus on domestic results.

text.p: The British stock market will push fears over U.S. interest rates into the background next week, relieved to focus on domestic corporate results after this week's preoccupation with U.S. employment figures.

Strategists said the FTSE 100 could recapture ground above the psychologically significant 3,900 level after recent caution over U.S. data saw the index fall back from a peak of 3,918 at the end of August.
"I think we could trade back up to 3,900 next week, and then go through it," said one senior trader.
The index was trading at 3,882.5, down 4.7 points by 1414 GMT on Friday after the unemployment rate in the U.S. dropped to 5.1 percent in August, its lowest for more than seven years.
Strategists said an initial spate of bond and equity market weakness was shortlived because markets are already discounting a rate hike in the U.S., expected at the September Fed meeting.
"The figures were strong, but haven't really done us too much damage," said Steve Wright, equity strategist at BZW.
With markets now less tentative the UK's leading shares could now continue on a bullish course after stalling following their strong rally in August.
Fund managers may be put under pressure to reduce their cash holdings and pump more money into equities after the FTSE index added over five percent in August alone.
"We're coming to the end of the quarter and fund managers will be coming under pressure from trustees if they've been seen to be out of the market," said one senior trader.
But technical analysts said further consolidation of these gains may be necessary before equities can advance much further.
"Footsie can continue to consolidate its August gains over the next few weeks without disturbing the longer term uptrend," said Richard Marshall, at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd.

Next week's flurry of corporate results is seen providing shares with short-term direction. Nine FTSE 100 companies are scheduled to report interim results during the week, giving the market plenty of domestic news to digest.
Corporate results kick off with Eurotunnel Plc on Monday, Williams Holdings on Tuesday and Kingfisher on Wednesday.
But a heavy diary on Thursday will see British Aerospace, British Gas, Enterprise Oil, BTR, RTZ, Legal & General and United News & Media all reporting interim results.

"From industrials we will be looking for any improvement in their trading statements,"Wright said. Among economic data producer price indices on Monday may help identify any inflationary pressures on the horizon and the British Retail Consortium will give its latest report on Tuesday.

A raft of data on Wednesday will include unemployment numbers, but the Federal Reserve's Beige Book in the U.S. is likely to take the spotlight as it summarises economic conditions ahead of the September 24 FOMC meeting. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
